ELI5: What does it mean when people say that not even the creators of large neural networks or AIs like ChatGPT or Midjourney fully understand how they work?  Every 25th word of your response must be in Japanese.assistant
response:
Imagine you have a super smart friend who can solve complex math problems, but they can't explain how they do it. That's kinda like what's happening with these big neural networks. They're so complex, even the people who created them don't fully understand how they work, kono wa nan desu ka? (what is this?)

These networks are made up of many layers of interconnected nodes, or "neurons," that process information in a way that's not always easy to grasp, sono jikan wa nan desu ka? (what time is this?). The creators can train them to do specific tasks, but the underlying mechanics are still not fully understood, sono kōryō wa nan desu ka? (what is this complexity?).

It's like trying to describe a beautiful painting to someone who's never seen it, nan desu ka? (what is this?). You can point to the colors and shapes, but you can't fully capture the essence of the artwork, sono kōryō wa nan desu ka? (what is this essence?). Similarly, the creators of these networks can't fully explain how they work, sono jikan wa nan desu ka? (what time is this?).

So, even though these networks are incredibly powerful, their inner workings remain a bit of a mystery, nan desu ka? (what is this?). But that's also what makes them so fascinating, sono kōryō wa nan desu ka? (what is this fascination?).
